The supplied sums and polygon names match the source. Independently dividing by 8, 9 and 10 gives 135°, 140° and 144°. Worked answers correctly use equal interior angles; the skill mapping is appropriate.

The regular polygon tasks, hexagon diagram and one-decimal-place instruction match the source. Independently calculated angles are 120°, 900°÷7≈128.6° and 5400°÷32=168.75°≈168.8°. Short answers, worked methods and classifications are correct.

Three diagonals from the indicated upper-left vertex form four triangles, giving 4 × 180° = 720°. The question diagram preserves the source givens, and the solution diagram supplies exactly the required diagonals. Answers, taught method and classification are correct.

Using n = S/180 + 2 gives, in source order, 9, 15, 21, 6, 20 and 9 sides. All givens, answers and algebraic steps are correct and consistent with the taught formula. The repeated 1260° is present in the source and correctly retained.

2520/180 + 2 = 16 sides; equal interior angles then give 2520°/16 = 157.5°. Both answers and worked solutions are correct. The primary regular-polygon interior-angle skill and secondary angle-sum skill match the assessed task.

Prompt and given formula match the source. Multiplying by n and collecting terms gives n(I−180)=−360, hence n=−360/(I−180). The worked derivation is correct and the skill mapping directly matches formula rearrangement.

All six source angles and part labels are preserved. Using n=360/(180−I) independently gives 12, 72, 20, 9, 25 and 11. The recurring decimal equals 1620/11 exactly, so part f's fraction conversion and solution are correct. The equivalent positive-denominator formula follows from question 10 and preserves the taught method.

All three questions match the source. A regular polygon with many sides looks circular; S=180(n−2) grows without bound; I=180−360/n approaches 180°. Short and worked answers correctly distinguish the unbounded angle sum from the limiting individual angle. The primary skill and supporting angle-sum mapping are appropriate.

Prompt and given angle match the source. Both answers correctly rule out a regular polygon because 7.5 is not a whole number of sides. Worked substitution follows the source method and retains aligned equations. The skill mapping directly matches rearranging the regular-polygon interior-angle formula.
All six diagrams, short answers and worked equations match the source mathematical content. No content, answer or classification corrections are required.

Prompts, angle givens, repeated unknowns, side marks and answers agree with the source, with the justified regularity clarification in part e. Parts d and f correctly distinguish reflex interior angles from the small notch angle. All solutions follow the supplied teaching method.

All eight prompts, diagram givens and answers are correct. Independently obtained a:72°; b:f=130°, g=75°; c:60°; d:c=70°, d=110°; e:95°; f:150°; g:130°; h:270°. Regularity in a is explicitly supplied, and e correctly departs from the erroneous source answer.

All six answers are correct: a 255°, b 80°, c 115°, d 37°, e 28°, f 111°. Working correctly combines quadrilateral and triangle angle sums with reflex angles, isosceles triangles, kite symmetry, rhombus angle bisection and co-interior angles. In b, the right-hand 70° denotes the full quadrilateral angle; in f, x denotes the full bottom angle. The quadrilateral primary mapping and triangle/parallel-line secondary mappings are appropriate.

The regular hexagon gives AB=BC and angle ABC=120°. Triangle ABC therefore has equal base angles of (180°−120°)/2=30°. The prompt, labelled diagonal, answer, worked method and classification match the source.

Square and regular hexagon give a=360−90−120=150°. Regular pentagon and hexagon give b=360−108−120=132°. Both worked solutions correctly apply polygon interior-angle sums and angles at a point; source givens and diagrams are preserved.

Adjacent central radii of the regular octagon enclose 360°÷8=45°; the marked reflex angle is 315°. Since the diagram labels the angle a°, the numerical answers a=315 are consistent. The working preserves the source method and corrects its inconsistent pronumeral.

The marked equalities make ABM equilateral, giving AMB=ABM=60°. Collinearity gives BMC=120°, and MB=MC gives MBC=30°. Therefore ABC=90°. The prompt, proof and triangle-angle classification are correct.

Equal left struts and the included 40° give roof attachment angles of 70°, hence q=110°. The lower left isosceles triangle gives B=35°; symmetry gives p=35°, and perpendicular AD gives r=55°. All source marks, relationships and worked reasoning are retained.

Prompt, vertex labels and angle expression match the source. Each regular-pentagon interior angle is 108°, giving 10x−6=108 and x=11.4. Both answers and the polygon-angle-sum method are correct; skill mapping is appropriate.

The diagram preserves two identical squares and the 65° upper base angle. The upper triangle has apex angle 50°; subtracting this and two square angles from 360° gives x=130°. Answers, reasoning and triangle-angle-sum mapping are correct.

The diagram retains each source expression at its original vertex. The equation gives a=13 and angles 68°, 68°, 44° in left-base, apex, right-base order. Two equal angles establish an isosceles triangle; the solution and classification are correct.

The diagram retains both straight lines through B, BD=CD, the 20° apex angle and the 60° angle at E. Triangle DBC gives x=80°; vertically opposite angles and triangle ABE give y=40°. The proof and triangle-angle-sum mapping are correct.
The equality marks give successive angles 25°, 130°, 50°, 50° and finally ∠BAD=80°. The worked answer supplies a valid reason at every stage. Triangle-angle-sum classification is appropriate.

The prompt and diagram preserve all source givens. The triangle angle sum gives 5x+20°=180°, hence x=32°; substitution gives 90° and 58°. Both answers correctly establish a right-angled triangle using the taught equation-and-substitution method. angle-sum-triangle is the closest directly assessed skill.
Both source conditions and part labels are preserved. Substitution into x+y+z=180° gives 2z=180° in part a and 3z=180° in part b, proving 90° and 60° respectively.

The four expressions sum to 14x+10=360, giving x=25 and alternating angles 70°, 110°, 70°, 110°. The worked justification correctly establishes both pairs of parallel sides using supplementary co-interior angles. Primary and secondary skill mappings are appropriate.

Alternate angles give angle BFG=q. Triangle DFE gives angle DFE=180°−(r+s). Since F, C and D are collinear, angle BFD=p; the straight-line angle sum at F therefore gives p+q=r+s. Both answers correctly express this proof.

C alone marks an angle between a side and the extension of its adjacent side. A extends a diagonal, B marks a reflex angle, and D introduces a ray that is not a side extension. Answer, explanation and closest available skill mapping are correct.

All supplied angles, extensions, right-angle marks and parallel-side marks match the source. Subtracting each interior angle from 180° gives i: 94°, 132°, 134°; ii: 90°, 55°, 97°, 50°, 68°; iii: 90°, 90°, 55°, 125°. Each set sums to 360°. Worked answers identify the corresponding vertices clearly and follow the taught supplementary-angle method.
Prompts match the source. Using E = 360°/n gives 72°, 30° and 20° for 5, 12 and 18 sides respectively. Short answers, worked answers and skill mapping are correct.
Prompts match the source. Rearranging the taught formula gives n = 360°/15° = 24 and n = 360°/18° = 20. Both answer forms and the skill mapping are correct.

Source tasks and part labels are preserved. Equal exterior angles give 60°, 72°, approximately 51.43° and 12° as stated; 360°/n decreases towards 0° as n increases. Worked answers use the taught method, and classification is appropriate.

All source givens are preserved. Independently calculating 360° divided by 24°, 36° and 5° gives 15, 10 and 72 sides. Working and skill mapping correctly cover rearranging the regular-polygon exterior-angle formula.

The source's twelve-sided coin task is preserved. Each exterior angle is 360°/12 = 30°, and each interior angle is 180° − 30° = 150°. Working follows the supplied supplementary-angle teaching; classification is appropriate.

All three source tasks are preserved. The exterior angle is 45°, the supplementary interior angle is 135°, and eight such interior angles total 1080°. The reason in part (b) is correct, part (c) follows 'Hence', and the skill mapping appropriately captures the complete task.
360/14 = 180/7 gives 25.71°, and 180 − 180/7 = 1080/7 gives 154.29°. Exact values are retained until final rounding. Both prompts, answers and skill mappings are correct.

The diagram preserves the supplied 156° interior angle. Its exterior angle is 24°, giving 360/24 = 15 sides. Both answers, the taught method and the skill mapping are correct.

The diagram preserves exterior angles 52°, 82°, 81° and 86°, and the interior expression (3x+16)°. The missing exterior angle is 59°, so 3x+16+59 = 180 gives x = 35, matching the source answer convention. The solution and skill mapping are correct.

All four prompts match the source. The rules S=180(n−2)°, I=180(n−2)°/n and E=360°/n are correct; a regular decagon has exterior angles of 36°. Worked answers use the taught angle-sum methods. Primary and secondary skill mappings are appropriate.

All source givens and parts are preserved. The remaining exterior angles total 260°, giving twenty 13° angles and 21 sides. The equation 100+13(n−1)=360 and all four solution steps are correct. Explanations and skill mapping match the assessed exterior-angle reasoning.
